nodes.title: the Tarnsib signature
nodes.statement: The Tarnsib system concerns objects called jenxils. There are exactly 3 of them: reldvint, wrenmux, zellum. One operation is written %. One relation is written =<, read as "shadows".

nodes.title: the Tarnsib combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x % y for every pair of jenxils is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the =< relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all jenxils x and y, x % y is again a jenxil.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every jenxil x: x =< x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all jenxils x and y: if x =< y and y =< x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all jenxils x, y, z: if x =< y and y =< z then x =< z.

nodes.title: comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: For all jenxils x and y, at least one of x =< y and y =< x holds.

nodes.title: the system does not have association of the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all jenxils x, y, z: (x % y) % z = x % (y % z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = wrenmux, y = reldvint, z = wrenmux, left = reldvint, right = wrenmux, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: yukwren jenxils
nodes.statement: A jenxil x is called yukwren when x % x = x.

nodes.title: jenxils that xilwren
nodes.statement: Two jenxils x and y are said to xilwren when x % y = y % x.

nodes.title: espagrix collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of jenxils is espagrix when x % y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the rastqen of a jenxil
nodes.statement: The rastqen of a jenxil x is the collection of jenxils y for which x =< y holds.

nodes.title: the glimlum
nodes.statement: The glimlum of the system is the collection of jenxils that xilwren with every jenxil.

nodes.title: the rastzam
nodes.statement: The rastzam is the collection of all yukwren jenxils.

nodes.title: the voropal of a jenxil
nodes.statement: The voropal of a jenxil x, written [x], is the smallest espagrix collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a wrenwren
nodes.statement: A jenxil f is a wrenwren when f =< y holds for every jenxil y, that is, when the rastqen of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: the muxhob of a jenxil
nodes.statement: The muxhob of a jenxil x is the number of jenxils in its voropal [x].

nodes.title: the shenfal
nodes.statement: The shenfal of the system is the collection of jenxils whose muxhob is largest.

nodes.title: iskclo pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct jenxils x and y form a iskclo pair when x =< y and y =< x both hold, that is, when each lies in the rastqen of the other.

nodes.title: the voropal of a jenxil is espagrix
nodes.statement: For every jenxil x, the collection [x] is espagrix.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under %.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the voropal is contained in every espagrix collection
nodes.statement: If S is espagrix and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a jenxil is yukwren exactly when its muxhob is one
nodes.statement: x % x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x % x = x then {x} is already closed under %.
So [x] = {x} and the muxhob is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x % x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the muxhob divides the number of jenxils breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every jenxil x, the muxhob of x divides 3.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = wrenmux, reach = 2, size = 3, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the rastzam is espagrix
nodes.statement: If x and y are both yukwren then so is x % y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be yukwren.
The claim asks whether (x % y) % (x % y) returns x % y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: rastqens are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the rastqen of x, then the rastqen of y is contained in the rastqen of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x =< y and let z satisfy y =< z.
Transitivity gives x =< z.
So every member of the rastqen of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one wrenwren
nodes.statement: No two distinct jenxils can both be wrenwrens.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f =< h, since h is any object, and h =< f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the system has a wrenwren
nodes.statement: Some jenxil wrenwrens the whole system.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every pair is comparable, so the relation orders the objects into a line.
The claim is that the line has a bottom.
The carrier is finite, so the search over candidates terminates.

nodes.title: no iskclo pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct jenxils lie in each other's rastqen.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.
